page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained vCPU configuration. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores across 2 threads per core under Microsoft Hyper-V. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a substantial 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a local temporary 322 GB SSD. The configuration includes no discrete GPUs and operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core computational ability, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 2702.28 in the top quartile. However, overall multi-core computational throughput is constrained by the 4 vCPU cap, reflected in lower-tier results across PassMark CPU (6181.49), multi-core stress-ng (5399.28), and Geekbench multi-core (3646.0). Memory subsystems achieve average throughput for large read blocks at 39.33 GB/sec and an overall average PassMark memory score of 2462.52, while write throughput and cached block read bandwidth land in the lower quartile.

The qualitative tradeoff of the E8-4ads_v5 resides in its constrained core-to-memory architecture. By restricting the 8-vCPU chassis to 4 active vCPUs while retaining the full 64.0 GB memory footprint, this instance optimizes licensing costs for software billed on a per-core basis. It suits memory-heavy enterprise databases, in-memory caching, and data processing tasks requiring high memory capacity without the necessity for broad parallel compute resources.
description: Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for high-memory workloads with constrained compute footprints. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz, it provisions 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores alongside 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local temporary storage is provided via a 322 GB SSD, with no integrated GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks show strong single-core CPU throughput, while aggregate multi-core metrics and write-heavy memory bandwidth remain limited by the low core count. The server offers cost efficiency for applications with per-core licensing fees, making it suitable for relational database engines, in-memory caches, and enterprise data tasks requiring high memory allocation over raw thread count.
